text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident P1 detected — elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate in us-west-2 (service: inference-runtime). Paging the oncall.
alex chen: oncall here. I see the alert, jumping in. Can others confirm if this is a model-serving runtime regression or infra noise?
samir rao: looking at pod logs now. Seeing a spike of `kv-cache` OOMs right before the 5xx burst. Also noticed kernel-selection errors in the runtime: `failed to choose kernel for aten::matmul` around 20:03 UTC.
maya patel: I pushed a kernel heuristic change in the last rollout (rev: r-2026.03.12). Rolling that back to r-2026.03.09 now to test mitigation.
alex chen: rollback started. Redirecting traffic to warm fallback pool to reduce requests hitting the affected path. Monitoring dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/errors
elena (CS): tagging this for customer comms. Which customers saw impact? Any data exposure risk?
samir rao: quick customer impact assessment: majority of requests got 500s for ~15m window; errors hit both hosted API and dedicated routes in us-west-2 only. No logs indicate PII leakage — internal audit confirms no record writes affected.
status-bot: Draft status page update (suggestion):
```
Status: Degraded
Service: Text Generation (us-west-2)
Impact: Increased error rates and higher latency for /v1/generate. Some requests returned 500.
Current status: Mitigation in progress — rollback of recent runtime kernel heuristic. No evidence of customer data exposure.
ETA: monitoring; next update in 30 minutes.
```
elena (CS): draft customer email for review:
```
Hi <Customer>,

We experienced elevated errors impacting generation requests in us-west-2 between 20:03–20:18 UTC. Our oncall engineers applied a rollback and mitigation which restored normal service. We apologize for the disruption. No customer data was exposed.

We will follow up with a short RCA and next steps.

— Redwood Inference Support
```
cs-manager: Include which models/routes were affected and whether any ingested payloads were retried. Also propose an SLA credit line: "We will review and apply credits per our SLA where applicable."
alex chen: timeline for records: detection 20:03 UTC, mitigation initiated 20:06 UTC, rollback complete 20:18 UTC, error rate returned to baseline by ~20:25 UTC. Root cause preliminary: a regression in kernel-selection logic that mis-classified some attention/matmul paths under a specific sequence-length distribution.
maya patel: proposed preventive actions:
- revert heuristic (done)
- add unit/regression tests that synthesize the failing attention/matmul signature
- expand canary window and run kernel-selection tests during canary
- add an alert for sudden kv-cache OOMs tied to kernel errors
samir rao: internal RCA summary draft for customers: "A recent runtime optimization introduced a kernel-selection heuristic which, for a narrow set of request shapes, selected an incompatible execution kernel causing memory handling issues and 5xx responses. The patch has been reverted and additional tests and canary checks are scheduled."
elena (CS): can we confirm the list of affected regions and customers? I want to include per-customer impact in the email thread before sending.
samir rao: affected region: us-west-2 only. Affected customers: those with active traffic routed to hosted endpoints in us-west-2 between 20:00–20:30 UTC. I can pull a per-customer hit count — will attach CSV to the followup.
cs-manager: ok, we'll prepare two emails: (1) immediate notice to all customers in us-west-2; (2) personalized follow-up to customers with >100 failed requests including estimated credit. Elena, draft both; Samir attach counts.
elena (CS): will draft now. Quick approval question: can we say "no data exposed"? Need ops to confirm.
alex chen: ops confirmed — no persistence or external calls were affected. Safe to say no data exposure.
elena (CS): email approved. Sending first broadcast now. Will post copy to #customer-success for records.
alex chen: internal post-incident comms (short):
```
Incident: P1 — us-west-2 /v1/generate 5xx spike
Root cause: kernel-selection regression in runtime
Mitigation: rollback to r-2026.03.09 and traffic routing to fallback pool
Status: resolved, monitoring
Action items: add regression tests, extend canary, alert for kv-cache OOMs
Owners: maya (runtime), samir (infra), alex (oncall)
```
maya patel: I'll open a PR with the regression test and link the canary config change. ETA EOD.
samir rao: attaching preliminary per-customer counts (will upload CSV to the ticket). Also creating an ops ticket to add the new alert: OPS-4021.
cs-manager: thanks team. Elena — schedule follow-up email with RCA + exact timeline tomorrow AM. Include credit resolution process.
elena (CS): will prepare final RCA summary and CC account teams. Draft to be reviewed in #customer-success by 09:30 UTC tomorrow.
oncall-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged closed. Summary uploaded to incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-0382
alex chen: closing loop here. If anyone finds further anomalies on the metric, ping me. :thumbsup:
